name: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
authors: Lin, Wang, Tang, Han, Chen, Yang, Wu
problem: Weight-only quantization to 3-4 bits either degrades quality badly or requires expensive per-channel/group grid search at quantization time; naive round-to-nearest INT4 is much worse than RTN at INT8.
mechanism: Protect a small subset (~1%) of weight channels that are salient in the ACTIVATION distribution rather than the weight distribution: score each input channel by the mean magnitude of its activations across calibration data, scale the salient channels up by a per-channel factor s, quantize with per-group asymmetric INT3/INT4 grids, and fold s into the preceding LayerNorm so no extra runtime cost. Grid scales chosen by a search that minimises the output reconstruction error weighted by activation magnitude.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract + tables 1-5, MLsys 2024 Best Paper): near-lossless W4 (group size 128) on LLaMA/LLaMA-2 families with 3.6x smaller weights, plus 4-bit models fitting on a single 24GB-class GPU; measured decode speedup 1.7-3.9x over FP16 on the same GPU. COMPRESSION RATIO: ~4x weight compression (16 -> 4 bit, g128). QUALITY COST: INT4-g128 WikiText perplexity is within noise of FP16 for most LLaMA models; INT3-g128 is NOT - the perplexity gap widens sharply there, which the paper reports rather than hides.
